# Build the epiloYES UI from the design canvas

## Context

You have a 26-artboard Claude Design canvas, **"epiloYES in evreos"**
(`claude.ai/code/artifact/059a20a9-…`, updated 2026-09-04), and you are satisfied
with it. It is the first complete visual design this project has ever had in one
place. This plan turns it into buildable work.

Three facts shape everything below.

**1. The canvas is the only copy of the design, and it is outside the repository.**
Twenty-four call sites in the code cite mockups by ID — `Masthead.astro` "mockup 1a",
`ReaderLayout.astro` "the mockups' 1280 canvas", five commits on `xcoder/cashback-web`
reading "rebuild the wallet to mockup 4a (#229)". None of those mockups is in version
control; they live as attachments on GitHub issues. The vendored `modernist.css` names
an upstream design project (`_ds/modernist-2f5ef9ba-…/styles.css`) that does not exist
on this machine either. The design has been this repository's load-bearing missing
artifact for a month, and the canvas is the chance to end that.

**2. Most of the canvas is not this repository's work.** It draws epiloYES *inside the
evreos shell*. `docs/master-prompts/evreos-browser.md` opens: "Planning artifact only.
Nothing in this file is in scope for `apivo-news`." Your own annotation band agrees —
"THE SHELL — evreos's to build, ours only to assume". The buildable scope here is the
row you labelled **"THE FOUNDATIONAL SCREENS … None of these exists"**, plus the dark
theme, plus the seam recorded as a contract.

**3. Your checkout is 773 commits stale.** Local `main` is `7a20f38` (2026-08-24);
`origin/main` is `20de06c` (2026-09-04). Everything on disk predates the entire
cashback backend. `git pull --ff-only` is step zero.

## Decisions taken (2026-09-05)

1. **Shell artboards → contract only, here.** No shell code in `apivo-news`; the seam
   becomes an ADR and a contract document that is the evreos repo's input.
2. **PR #493 merges first**, canvas-vs-branch differences follow as small issues.
3. **Member auth is in scope** — it is the longest engineering pole.
4. **1 October holds.** Sequence backwards from the partner pilot; name the critical
   path and the cut list.

## Verified state of play

*(read out of `origin/main` and `origin/xcoder/cashback-web`, not the stale tree)*

| Area | Reality |
|---|---|
| Frontend | Astro 7 SSR, `@astrojs/node`, TS strictest. **No Tailwind, no islands, no state lib.** Tokens in `web/src/styles/modernist.css`; scoped `<style>` per page. Only client dep is `driver.js`. Forms are plain GET/POST. |
| Pages on `main` | 16: reader front page, article, setup, register+consent, about, four `editor/*`, three error pages, `go.ts`, `api/tour/[tour].ts`. |
| Cashback UI | **Not on `main`.** 8 screens + `OpsLayout` + 4 components + `i18n/cashback.ts` on `origin/xcoder/cashback-web` — open **PR #493**, ~9.7k lines. |
| Cashback backend | Fully on `main`: migrations `0010`–`0033`, `internal/cashback/{catalogue,clickout,earnings,networks,ops,payout,wallet}`, `internal/platform/{money,brand,events,scheduler}`. |
| Brand config | Real and load-bearing: `internal/platform/brand/brand.go` → generated `web/src/lib/brand/brand.types.ts`, loader `web/src/lib/brand/index.ts`. Carries `legal{entity,jurisdiction,address,documents}`, `support{general,legal,privacy}`, `assets{logo,logoDark,favicon}`, `theme{colours,typography}`. **Only the fictional "Zephyra" fixture brand exists — no real epiloYES `brand.json`, no logo, no favicon.** |
| Theme | Light only. `contrast.test.ts` parses `modernist.css` and asserts WCAG ratios — it reads the **first** match per token, so a dark block under a media query would leave it silently asserting the light values. |
| Member auth | **Not wired.** `signInWithPassword` appears once, in `editor/signin.astro`. No member sign-up, sign-in or session anywhere. |
| Consent | `web/src/lib/account/consent.ts` is built and tested — three purposes (`newsletter`, `analytics`, `product_news`), append-only dated records, revoke is a date not a delete. Its own header: *"No endpoint exists … This module is the seam."* |
| Legal pages | Do not exist. `SiteFooter.astro` still renders "Imprint · Privacy · Contact — *still owed*" as dead text and hardcodes the literal `epiloYES`. Issue **#64 is closed as completed** — wrongly. |
| Crawler gate | Global in `web/src/middleware.ts`: UA denylist, disallow-all `robots.txt`, `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` on every response. New pages inherit it. |

| Spec-kit | Live and driving the project. `001` (T001–T035), `002` (CB-T001–T147), `003-cashback-claims` (T148–T192, **branch-only**, blocked on a constitution amendment), `004-multi-network-linkwise` (T200–**T294**, **in flight: 9 done / 59 open**). Next free range: **T300+**. |
| Feature creation | `.specify/scripts/bash/create-new-feature.sh` creates `specs/NNN-slug/` only — it does **not** create a git branch, so `xcoder/<slug>` naming stays ours. |

---

## 1. Scope boundary

**26 artboards, three destinations.**

| Destination | Count | Boards |
|---|---|---|
| **Work in `apivo-news`** | **10** | SignIn, Profile, ProfileDesktop, Settings, Faq, LegalDesktop, Palette, Theme, plus the two redraw deltas rolled into #493 follow-ups |
| **Already built — delta only** | **9** | NewsMobile, NewsDesktop, ArticleMobile, ArticleDesktop (on `main`); WalletMobile, WalletDesktop, CatalogueMobile, CatalogueDesktop, MerchantMobile (on PR #493) |
| **evreos repo — contract input, not work here** | **7** | LauncherClosed, LauncherOpen, LauncherDesktop, HomeMobile, HomeDesktop, Assistant, AssistantDraft |
| **Document, not a screen** | 2 | Main (the seam contract), SettingsSeam (the ownership split) |

The seam contract, extracted from `Main.dc.html`, is seven items and belongs in a
document: `viewport {top,bottom,left,right}` insets the module pads by;
`identity {token}` the module **exchanges** for its own session; `theme {scheme,brand}`
plus a change event, with **no theme switch inside the module**; `axes {language,
place[]}` as two values and never a locale; `money {minor:int, currency}` formatted by
whoever displays it; `navigate/back` intents owned by the shell; `assistant.context`
handed up as a scoped bundle that never carries identity or a session token.

`SettingsSeam.dc.html` states the rule that keeps the two settings screens from
disagreeing: **the shell owns the person and the device; the module owns the reading
and the money.** Write that line down — it is the whole boundary.

## 2. Spec-kit structure

**One feature, one ADR, and a set of issues on existing milestones.** Four spec/plan/
research sets for work that is one coherent user-facing story would be overhead, not
rigour — but the dark theme genuinely depends on nothing and the seam is a decision
rather than a feature, so neither belongs inside the feature's dependency graph.

### Feature `005-member-surfaces` — the only new spec-kit feature

- Directory `specs/005-member-surfaces/`, branch **`xcoder/005-member-surfaces`**,
  tasks **T300 onwards** (004 ends at T294), new milestone **M6 — Member Surfaces &
  Launch Legal**.
- Create it with:
  ```sh
  sh .specify/scripts/bash/create-new-feature.sh --number 5 \
     --short-name 'member-surfaces' \
     'Member accounts, the legal notices and the settings that belong to the module'
  ```
  then `/speckit-specify`, `/speckit-clarify` (press on the founder decisions in §5),
  `/speckit-plan`, `/speckit-tasks`, `/speckit-analyze`, `/speckit-taskstoissues`.
- The canvas is the spec's primary input. Paste the artboard inventory and the
  annotation bands into `/speckit-specify` — your own band text is the requirement
  language.

### Not features

| Work | Shape | Milestone |
|---|---|---|
| Seam contract | `docs/adr/0006-module-shell-seam.md` + `specs/005-member-surfaces/contracts/shell-seam.md`. One PR. | — |
| Vendor the canvas | `docs/design/` — the 26 `.dc.html` files, `canvas.json`, and a `README.md` index mapping **board → route → old mockup id** so the 24 existing "mockup 1a"/"4a" comments finally resolve. One issue. | M5 |
| Dark theme | 4 issues (tokens, `contrast.test.ts` restructure, `prefers-color-scheme` + `data-theme`, brand theme wiring). Runs in parallel from day one; depends on nothing. | M5 |
| Real brand | `internal/platform/brand/testdata/…` is a fixture; a real `brand.json` + logo/favicon assets. `area:brand`. | M6 |
| #493 deltas | Issues raised after the merge, one per screen difference. | CB-M4 / CB-M5 |
| Reopen **#64** | It is closed as completed and the pages do not exist. Reopen and re-point at the 005 phase. | M6 |

## 3. Build order

Phases 0–2 and the dark theme are all independent of member auth — start them together
as parallel worktree agents on day one.

**Phase 0 — Brand truth.** *(blocks Phase 1; partly blocked on you)*
Real `brand.json` for epiloYES: name, domains, theme colours, typography, defaults,
payout descriptor — all facts you already have. `legal.*` and `support.*` land when you
supply them (§5.1). Logo, `logoDark` and favicon assets. Then remove the hardcoded
`epiloYES` literal from `web/src/components/SiteFooter.astro` and `Masthead.astro` and
read `brand.name` instead — the Rebrandability lint should have caught it and did not.

**Phase 1 — The legal three.** *(the hard launch blocker)*
`/{lang}/impressum`, `/{lang}/privacy`, `/{lang}/contact` in `el` and `de`, every field
read from `brand.legal.*` / `brand.support.*` exactly as `LegalDesktop.dc.html` labels
them. `SiteFooter.astro` links them instead of naming them pending. Reopen #64; its
acceptance criteria are still the right ones.

**Phase 2 — FAQ.** *(cheap, no dependencies)*
`/{lang}/faq`. Your board states the rule: *"the answers are the same sentences that
already appear on the screens — if we said something different here, one of the two
would be wrong."* Build it so that is enforced: the FAQ imports the same string
constants the screens use, and a test asserts identity rather than similarity.
Cut the "the evreos assistant sees your screen" closing line — that shell does not exist.

**Phase 3 — Member session.** *(the longest pole; everything account-shaped waits here)*
Supabase magic-link auth for members. `web/src/lib/account/session.ts` mirroring the
shape of `web/src/lib/editorial/session.ts` (middleware resolves once per request, the
module maps claims), reusing `csrf.ts` and `secure-request.ts`. `/{lang}/signin` per
`SignIn.dc.html`, and the front page's disabled `signInPending` button becomes real.
The board's "Continue with evreos" path is drawn for later — build the email path now
and record the token exchange in the seam contract.

**Phase 4 — Profile and Settings.**
`/{lang}/profile` and `/{lang}/settings`. Reading language and places reuse
`web/src/lib/reader/preference.ts` and link to the existing `/setup` rather than
duplicating it. The consent panel reuses `web/src/lib/account/consent.ts` and the
existing panel in `register.astro` — but needs **new Go endpoints**, because that
module's own header says no endpoint exists. Payout destination reads the cashback
wallet. Push notifications render as a marked sketch, exactly as you drew them; do not
scaffold a service worker.

**Phase 5 — GDPR actions.** *(cuttable — see §6)*
Data export and account deletion, with their Go endpoints and the retention schedule.

**Phase 6 — Dark theme.** *(parallel from day one, not last)*
The `Palette` and `Theme` boards. Add the dark token block, restructure
`contrast.test.ts` so it evaluates **both** themes — today it takes the first match per
token name and would assert the light values against a dark palette without failing.

### The 1 October critical path

26 days. In order of lead time, longest first:

1. **Your Impressum facts** (§5.1) — the longest lead time is you, not the code.
   Everything else in Phase 1 is a day's work once they arrive.
2. **Member auth** (Phase 3) — the longest engineering pole, and the pilot cohort
   cannot have a wallet without it.
3. **PR #493 merged** — the wallet, catalogue, merchant and withdrawal screens the
   cohort actually touches.
4. **German copy throughout.** The cohort is German-speaking, 40+. The canvas is drawn
   in Greek; every new screen needs its `de` strings written, not translated late.
5. **Real brand + assets** (Phase 0).

## 4. Per-screen task shape

Every new screen is the same six commits, small and independently reviewable:

1. Strings module + its `.test.ts` (`web/src/lib/account/strings.ts` for the account
   surfaces, `web/src/lib/legal/strings.ts` for the legal three), `el` and `de`,
   keyed by the language axis — never a locale.
2. Add the new logic module to the `coverage.include` allowlist in
   `web/vitest.config.ts`; it is an explicit allowlist and new files are invisible to
   the 80% gate until listed.
3. The `.astro` page, taking every colour, space, radius and shadow from
   `modernist.css` variables and hardcoding none.
4. Any Go endpoint, with its migration and the test asserting the **database** refuses
   the illegal state (Principle VIII).
5. Wire it into `SiteFooter.astro` / navigation.
6. A `data-tour` anchor if the screen joins a tour — `web/src/lib/tour/tours.ts` is the
   flow map, and its own rule is that steps name elements by `data-tour`, never by class.

Reuse rather than rewrite: `reader/preference.ts` (axes cookie), `account/consent.ts`
(consent history), `editorial/session.ts` (session shape), `csrf.ts`,
`secure-request.ts`, `brand/index.ts`, and the consent panel already rendered in
`register.astro`.

## 5. Founder decisions still owed

**Blocking launch (supply these first — they are the critical path):**

1. **Impressum facts** — legal entity name and form, registered address,
   represented-by, register and number, VAT id, and the §18 MStV responsible person for
   editorial content. *Blocks: Phase 1, and therefore public launch.* No default exists;
   these are business facts.
2. **Retention schedule** — deferred in the 001 clarifications and owed before launch.
   *Blocks: the privacy page's content and Phase 5's deletion behaviour.*
3. **Controller identity and whether a DPO is required.** *Blocks: the privacy page.*
4. **Brand assets** — logo, `logoDark`, favicon. *Blocks: Phase 0 completion.*

**Blocking engineering (needed to start, defaults exist):**

5. **Member sign-in method.** Default: **Supabase magic link**, because the board's
   "Continue with evreos" path needs a shell that does not exist, and a password for a
   40+ cohort is friction the pilot does not need.
6. **Default language for the pilot cohort.** The canvas is drawn in Greek; the
   Orthopelma cohort is German. Default: `brand.defaults.language = 'de'` for the pilot
   brand, with Greek fully available — the two axes are independent, which is the point.
7. **Does the FAQ keep its assistant line?** Default: cut it until evreos exists.

## 6. Risks and the cut order

**Cut in this order if 1 October gets tight:**
1. GDPR self-service export/deletion (Phase 5) → the privacy page names
   `brand.support.privacy` as the address to write to. GDPR requires you to *honour* a
   request within a month, not to have a button. This is an honest cut; say so on the page.
2. Dark theme (Phase 6) → ships after the pilot.
3. `ProfileDesktop` refinements → mobile-first is right for this cohort anyway.
4. FAQ (Phase 2) → the answers already exist on the screens.

**Never cut:** the legal three, member auth, and the German copy. A German-facing money
surface without an Impressum and a privacy notice is not a scope decision.

**Risks:**
- **`contrast.test.ts` reads the first match per token.** A dark block added under a
  media query leaves the suite green while asserting the wrong palette. Restructure the
  parser before adding a single dark token.
- **Archivo ships no Greek subset** (issue #51) — Greek falls through to `system-ui`.
  The canvas is drawn in Greek, so the browser will not look like the artboards for
  Greek readers. Decide whether that is acceptable or a font is procured.
- **Issue #64 is closed as completed and is not done.** Anything else audited from
  closed issues may be equally wrong.
- **Consent has no endpoint.** The Settings consent panel looks like a read of existing
  work and is actually new backend.
- **The design has no upstream.** Vendor the canvas into `docs/design/` early — if the
  artifact is lost, the design is lost.
- **13 worktrees pinned to old `xcoder/cb-*` branches** and a 773-commit-stale tree.
  Clean these up before dispatching parallel agents, or they will branch from history.
- `docs/demo-recording-prompt.md` is untracked and would be lost by `git clean`.

## 7. Verification

- `git pull --ff-only` first, then `make vet && make test-unit`.
- Frontend gate as CI runs it: `cd web && npm ci && npm run check && npm test && npm run build`.
  The 80% vitest thresholds fail the build; new logic modules must be in the
  `coverage.include` allowlist or they are not measured.
- `npx vitest run src/styles/contrast.test.ts` after every token change, and confirm it
  actually evaluates the dark palette rather than re-reading the light one.
- The fixture-brand render test proves rebrandability; run it against the new legal and
  account pages — every field must come from `brand.*`, which is exactly how the
  `LegalDesktop` board is annotated.
- Confirm the crawler gate covers the new routes: every response carries
  `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` from `web/src/middleware.ts` — #64's last acceptance
  criterion.
- Docker is broken on this machine and left alone by choice: **CI is the verification of
  record.** Every PR must state which checks ran locally and which ran in CI.
- Branches are `xcoder/<slug>`, Conventional Commits referencing the issue, one PR per
  issue, signed, no AI attribution anywhere. `make ref-lint` and
  `sh scripts/lint-refs.sh --from-messages origin/main..HEAD` before pushing.

#!/bin/sh
# Brand-literal lint — ADR-0004, FR-070, constitution "Rebrandability".
#
# A rebrand must be a configuration change plus an asset swap. That is only
# true if no product name, domain, support address or colour is written into
# application code, templates or migrations, so this greps the tracked tree
# for the current brand's literals and fails on a hit that is not accounted
# for.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# WHAT IS OUT OF SCOPE, AND WHY
#
# Whole path classes are skipped because FR-070 is about application code,
# templates and migrations:
#
#   docs/ specs/ .specify/ README.md   Documentation and history. The ADR
#                                      names these as the genuine references
#                                      an allowlist has to make room for: a
#                                      changelog cannot be rebranded, it
#                                      records what was true at the time.
#   .github/ deploy/                   Deployment and CI configuration. Host
#                                      names there address infrastructure,
#                                      not members, and a rebrand changes
#                                      them by changing the deployment.
#   internal/platform/brand/           The brand configuration itself and its
#   web/src/lib/brand/                 two readers. This is where the
#                                      literals are SUPPOSED to be.
#   scripts/lint-brand-literals.sh     This file, which has to name what it
#   scripts/lint-brand-literals_test.sh  forbids in order to forbid it, and
#                                      its tests, which have to write the
#                                      forbidden thing down to prove it is
#                                      caught.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# THE BUDGET TABLE, AND WHAT IT IS NOT
#
# The tree already carries brand literals: this repository shipped a news
# product before it had a brand configuration, and its surfaces render the
# product name directly. Driving those to zero is issue #275. Until then the
# table below records, per file, exactly how many hits are known and
# accepted — frozen at the state of the tree on the day this lint landed.
#
# That is a ratchet, not an amnesty. A file over its budget FAILS, so a new
# literal cannot be added to an already-listed file; a file with no budget
# fails on its first hit, so a new file cannot introduce one at all. A file
# under its budget only warns, so removing a literal never breaks somebody
# else's pull request — it just leaves a note asking for the number to come
# down with it.
#
# The patterns are deliberately not weakened to make the table shorter.
set -eu

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" || exit 1

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT INT TERM
hits="$work/hits"
: > "$hits"

# The brand's proper nouns, domains, addresses and colours. Every pattern is
# matched case-insensitively: an upper-case hex colour is still a colour, and
# a product name is still the product name however it is capitalised.
#
# Word boundaries are written out as POSIX ERE - "followed by something that
# is not more of the same, or by the end of the line" - rather than with \b.
# \b is a GNU extension that git's regex engine may or may not provide
# depending on how it was built, and a lint whose verdict depends on the
# contributor's machine is a lint nobody can act on.
NAME_PATTERN='epiloyes'
HOST_PATTERN='[a-z0-9._%+-]*@?(apivo|epiloyes)\.(com|net|org|news|app|io|eu|de|gr|example)([^a-z0-9]|$)'

- **The design has no upstream.** Vendor the canvas into `docs/design/` early — if the
  artifact is lost, the design is lost.
- **13 worktrees pinned to old `xcoder/cb-*` branches** and a 773-commit-stale tree.
  Clean these up before dispatching parallel agents, or they will branch from history.
- `docs/demo-recording-prompt.md` is untracked and would be lost by `git clean`.

- `git pull --ff-only` first, then `make vet && make test-unit`.

  `coverage.include` allowlist or they are not measured.

  That is the mechanism that makes the `LegalDesktop` board's `brand.legal.entity` /
  `brand.support.legal` annotations true rather than aspirational. The fixture-brand render
  test is the other half: run it against every new legal and account page.
- Confirm the crawler gate covers the new routes: every response carries
  `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` from `web/src/middleware.ts` — #64's last acceptance
  criterion.
- Docker is broken on this machine and left alone by choice: **CI is the verification of
  record.** Every PR must state which checks ran locally and which ran in CI.
- Branches are `xcoder/<slug>`, Conventional Commits referencing the issue, one PR per
  issue, signed, no AI attribution anywhere. `make ref-lint` and
  `sh scripts/lint-refs.sh --from-messages origin/main..HEAD` before pushing.

  Launch Legal**.
- Create it with:
  ```sh
  sh .specify/scripts/bash/create-new-feature.sh --number 5 \
     --short-name 'member-surfaces' \
     'Member accounts, the legal notices and the settings that belong to the module'
  ```
  then `/speckit-specify`, `/speckit-clarify` (press on the founder decisions in §5),
  `/speckit-plan`, `/speckit-tasks`, `/speckit-analyze`, `/speckit-taskstoissues`.
- The canvas is the spec's primary input. Your annotation bands are the requirement
  language — use them verbatim. A per-screen inventory (every element, state, string
  key and `brand.*` field on all 26 boards, each grounded against the real repository)
  is being extracted now by a background swarm; it lands as the body of
  `/speckit-specify` rather than as anything you need to read to approve this plan.

### Not features

| Work | Shape | Milestone |
|---|---|---|
| Seam contract | `docs/adr/0006-module-shell-seam.md` + `specs/005-member-surfaces/contracts/shell-seam.md`. One PR. | — |
| Vendor the canvas | `docs/design/` — the 26 `.dc.html` files, `canvas.json`, and a `README.md` index mapping **board → route → old mockup id** so the 24 existing "mockup 1a"/"4a" comments finally resolve. One issue. | M5 |
| Dark theme | 4 issues (tokens, `contrast.test.ts` restructure, `prefers-color-scheme` + `data-theme`, brand theme wiring). Runs in parallel from day one; depends on nothing. | M5 |
| Real brand | `internal/platform/brand/testdata/…` is a fixture; a real `brand.json` + logo/favicon assets. `area:brand`. | M6 |
| #493 deltas | Issues raised after the merge, one per screen difference. | CB-M4 / CB-M5 |
| Reopen **#64** | It is closed as completed and the pages do not exist. Reopen and re-point at the 005 phase. | M6 |

## 3. Build order

Phases 0–2 and the dark theme are all independent of member auth — start them together
as parallel worktree agents on day one.

**Phase 0 — Brand truth.** *(blocks Phase 1; partly blocked on you)*
Real `brand.json` for epiloYES: name, domains, theme colours, typography, defaults,
payout descriptor — all facts you already have. `legal.*` and `support.*` land when you
supply them (§5.1). Logo, `logoDark` and favicon assets.

`scripts/lint-brand-literals.sh` already governs this and is a **ratchet, not a gate**:
thirteen existing files carry budgeted `epiloYES` literals — `SiteFooter.astro 1`,
`about.astro 2`, `404/500/503.astro 2` each — frozen the day the lint landed, with
issue **#275** tracking them to zero. Two consequences worth knowing before writing a
line: a file **with no budget fails on its first hit**, so every new page in this plan
must be literal-free from its first commit; and reducing an existing budget only warns,
so folding `SiteFooter.astro` onto `brand.name` is safe to do alongside Phase 1.

**Phase 1 — The legal three.** *(the hard launch blocker)*
`/{lang}/impressum`, `/{lang}/privacy`, `/{lang}/contact` in `el` and `de`, every field
read from `brand.legal.*` / `brand.support.*` exactly as `LegalDesktop.dc.html` labels
them. `SiteFooter.astro` links them instead of naming them pending. Reopen #64; its
acceptance criteria are still the right ones.

**Phase 2 — FAQ.** *(cheap, no dependencies)*
`/{lang}/faq`. Your board states the rule: *"the answers are the same sentences that
already appear on the screens — if we said something different here, one of the two
would be wrong."* Build it so that is enforced: the FAQ imports the same string
constants the screens use, and a test asserts identity rather than similarity.
Cut the "the evreos assistant sees your screen" closing line — that shell does not exist.

**Phase 3 — Member session.** *(the longest pole; everything account-shaped waits here)*
Supabase magic-link auth for members. `web/src/lib/account/session.ts` mirroring the
shape of `web/src/lib/editorial/session.ts` (middleware resolves once per request, the
module maps claims), reusing `csrf.ts` and `secure-request.ts`. `/{lang}/signin` per
`SignIn.dc.html`, and the front page's disabled `signInPending` button becomes real.
The board's "Continue with evreos" path is drawn for later — build the email path now
and record the token exchange in the seam contract.

**Phase 4 — Profile and Settings.**
`/{lang}/profile` and `/{lang}/settings`. Reading language and places reuse
`web/src/lib/reader/preference.ts` and link to the existing `/setup` rather than
duplicating it. The consent panel reuses `web/src/lib/account/consent.ts` and the
existing panel in `register.astro` — but needs **new Go endpoints**, because that
module's own header says no endpoint exists. Payout destination reads the cashback
wallet. Push notifications render as a marked sketch, exactly as you drew them; do not
scaffold a service worker.

**Phase 5 — GDPR actions.** *(cuttable — see §6)*
Data export and account deletion, with their Go endpoints and the retention schedule.

**Phase 6 — Dark theme.** *(parallel from day one, not last)*
The `Palette` and `Theme` boards. Add the dark token block, restructure
`contrast.test.ts` so it evaluates **both** themes — today it takes the first match per
token name and would assert the light values against a dark palette without failing.

### The 1 October critical path

26 days. In order of lead time, longest first:

1. **Your Impressum facts** (§5.1) — the longest lead time is you, not the code.
   Everything else in Phase 1 is a day's work once they arrive.
2. **Member auth** (Phase 3) — the longest engineering pole, and the pilot cohort
   cannot have a wallet without it.
3. **PR #493 merged** — the wallet, catalogue, merchant and withdrawal screens the
   cohort actually touches.
4. **German copy throughout.** The cohort is German-speaking, 40+. The canvas is drawn
   in Greek; every new screen needs its `de` strings written, not translated late.
5. **Real brand + assets** (Phase 0).

## 4. Per-screen task shape

Every new screen is the same six commits, small and independently reviewable:

1. Strings module + its `.test.ts` (`web/src/lib/account/strings.ts` for the account
   surfaces, `web/src/lib/legal/strings.ts` for the legal three), `el` and `de`,
   keyed by the language axis — never a locale.
2. Add the new logic module to the `coverage.include` allowlist in
   `web/vitest.config.ts`; it is an explicit allowlist and new files are invisible to
   the 80% gate until listed.
3. The `.astro` page, taking every colour, space, radius and shadow from
   `modernist.css` variables and hardcoding none.
4. Any Go endpoint, with its migration and the test asserting the **database** refuses
   the illegal state (Principle VIII).
5. Wire it into `SiteFooter.astro` / navigation.
6. A `data-tour` anchor if the screen joins a tour — `web/src/lib/tour/tours.ts` is the
   flow map, and its own rule is that steps name elements by `data-tour`, never by class.

Reuse rather than rewrite: `reader/preference.ts` (axes cookie), `account/consent.ts`
(consent history), `editorial/session.ts` (session shape), `csrf.ts`,
`secure-request.ts`, `brand/index.ts`, and the consent panel already rendered in
`register.astro`.

## 5. Founder decisions still owed

**Blocking launch (supply these first — they are the critical path):**

1. **Impressum facts** — legal entity name and form, registered address,
   represented-by, register and number, VAT id, and the §18 MStV responsible person for
   editorial content. *Blocks: Phase 1, and therefore public launch.* No default exists;
   these are business facts.
2. **Retention schedule** — deferred in the 001 clarifications and owed before launch.
   *Blocks: the privacy page's content and Phase 5's deletion behaviour.*
3. **Controller identity and whether a DPO is required.** *Blocks: the privacy page.*
4. **Brand assets** — logo, `logoDark`, favicon. *Blocks: Phase 0 completion.*

**Blocking engineering (needed to start, defaults exist):**

5. **Member sign-in method.** Default: **Supabase magic link**, because the board's
   "Continue with evreos" path needs a shell that does not exist, and a password for a
   40+ cohort is friction the pilot does not need.
6. **Default language for the pilot cohort.** The canvas is drawn in Greek; the
   Orthopelma cohort is German. Default: `brand.defaults.language = 'de'` for the pilot
   brand, with Greek fully available — the two axes are independent, which is the point.
7. **Does the FAQ keep its assistant line?** Default: cut it until evreos exists.

## 6. Risks and the cut order

**Cut in this order if 1 October gets tight:**
1. GDPR self-service export/deletion (Phase 5) → the privacy page names
   `brand.support.privacy` as the address to write to. GDPR requires you to *honour* a
   request within a month, not to have a button. This is an honest cut; say so on the page.
2. Dark theme (Phase 6) → ships after the pilot.
3. `ProfileDesktop` refinements → mobile-first is right for this cohort anyway.
4. FAQ (Phase 2) → the answers already exist on the screens.

**Never cut:** the legal three, member auth, and the German copy. A German-facing money
surface without an Impressum and a privacy notice is not a scope decision.

**Risks:**
- **`contrast.test.ts` reads the first match per token.** A dark block added under a
  media query leaves the suite green while asserting the wrong palette. Restructure the
  parser before adding a single dark token.
- **Archivo ships no Greek subset** (issue #51) — Greek falls through to `system-ui`.
  The canvas is drawn in Greek, so the browser will not look like the artboards for
  Greek readers. Decide whether that is acceptable or a font is procured.
- **Issue #64 is closed as completed and is not done.** Anything else audited from
  closed issues may be equally wrong.
- **Consent has no endpoint.** The Settings consent panel looks like a read of existing
  work and is actually new backend.
- **The design has no upstream.** Vendor the canvas into `docs/design/` early — if the
  artifact is lost, the design is lost.
- **13 worktrees pinned to old `xcoder/cb-*` branches** and a 773-commit-stale tree.
  Clean these up before dispatching parallel agents, or they will branch from history.
- `docs/demo-recording-prompt.md` is untracked and would be lost by `git clean`.

## 7. Verification

- `git pull --ff-only` first, then `make vet && make test-unit`.
- Frontend gate as CI runs it: `cd web && npm ci && npm run check && npm test && npm run build`.
  The 80% vitest thresholds fail the build; new logic modules must be in the
  `coverage.include` allowlist or they are not measured.
- `npx vitest run src/styles/contrast.test.ts` after every token change, and confirm it
  actually evaluates the dark palette rather than re-reading the light one.
- `sh scripts/lint-brand-literals.sh` — new pages have no budget entry, so any product
  name, domain, support address or hex colour written into them fails on the first hit.
  That is the mechanism that makes the `LegalDesktop` board's `brand.legal.entity` /
  `brand.support.legal` annotations true rather than aspirational. The fixture-brand render
  test is the other half: run it against every new legal and account page.
- Confirm the crawler gate covers the new routes: every response carries
  `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` from `web/src/middleware.ts` — #64's last acceptance
  criterion.
- Docker is broken on this machine and left alone by choice: **CI is the verification of
  record.** Every PR must state which checks ran locally and which ran in CI.
- Branches are `xcoder/<slug>`, Conventional Commits referencing the issue, one PR per
  issue, signed, no AI attribution anywhere. `make ref-lint` and
  `sh scripts/lint-refs.sh --from-messages origin/main..HEAD` before pushing.

# Building the canvas: one pilot feature, one deferred design feature, three documents

**Date:** 2026-09-05 · **Repo:** apivo-news @ origin/main `20de06c` · **Canvas:** 26 artboards, "epiloYES in evreos"

Everything below was verified against `origin/main` (and `origin/xcoder/cashback-web` for PR #493) during this session. Where the three input proposals disagreed, the resolution is stated inline with the evidence.

Plan file: `C:\Users\madym\.claude\plans\so-now-that-i-m-drifting-waterfall-agent-ad9871e3f4862b588.md`

---

## 0. The five verified facts that decide the shape

| # | Fact | Verified by | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Member authentication already exists on the backend.** `internal/identity/{verifier,service,role}.go` verifies Supabase JWTs and resolves the subject to an `account` row; `internal/cashback/{wallet,clickout,catalogue,payout,ops}/auth.go` each gate every route behind a `MemberAuthenticator` that takes the member **from the token and never from the path**; `cmd/apivo/main.go` wires all of it. | `git ls-tree origin/main internal/identity/`, `internal/cashback/*/auth.go` | Proposal 3 is right and Proposals 1 and 2 are **wrong**: "member identity does not exist" is false. What is missing is the *frontend* half (a member session module) and *account-row provisioning*. That is days, not a feature. |
| 2 | **No production path inserts an `account` row.** `git grep "insert into account" origin/main -- internal` matches only `_test.go` files. `identity.ErrUnknownAccount` is documented as "authenticated with Supabase but was never provisioned here" → 401. | `git grep`, `internal/identity/service.go:16` | A member who signs up with Supabase today gets a valid token and a 401 everywhere. Provisioning is on the critical path. |
| 3 | **`BRAND_DIR` gates the money path.** `cmd/apivo/main.go:779` logs *"BRAND_DIR is unset, so this deployment has no brand definition: members cannot opt into cashback and POST /api/v1/cashback/participation will answer 503"*, and line 791 fails when the brand defines no terms document. | `cmd/apivo/main.go:763–795` | The legal documents are **not** a compliance chore beside the product; they are a precondition of opt-in, enforced today. This collapses "legal pages" and "brand seam" into one blocking prerequisite. |
| 4 | **`docs/adr/0005-cashback-stack.md` already exists.** | `git ls-tree origin/main docs/adr/` | Proposals 2 and 3 both proposed writing ADR **0005** — both wrong. Next free numbers are **0006** and **0007**. |
| 5 | **The pilot has a date.** `docs/master-prompts/evreos-browser.md`: *"The partner's new shop opens on 1 October and cannot wait for a browser. The pilot runs on the existing web surfaces."* Cohort: a German orthopaedic shop, thousands of patients, a partner-funded price-lock programme. | that file, lines ~37–45 | **26 days from today.** The canvas is a secondary artefact. |

Supporting facts also verified: `web/src/styles/modernist.css` contains **exactly 39** hex-bearing lines against a `scripts/lint-brand-literals.sh` budget of **exactly 39** (`awk` verdict `if (count > allowed) FAIL`); `web/src/styles/contrast.test.ts:16` uses `css.match(new RegExp(...))` — non-global, **first match wins**; `.specify/scripts/bash/create-new-feature.sh` contains **no `git checkout`** and only prints `export SPECIFY_FEATURE=` (spec-kit numbering is a directory label, not a git ref); `specs/` on main holds 001, 002, 004 (003 arrives with PR #493); 004 has **59 open / 9 done** tasks; `web/src/middleware.ts` serves disallow-all `robots.txt`, stamps `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`, and 403s crawler user-agents; `web/src/pages/[lang]/register.astro` has every field `disabled`; `wallet.astro:73` calls `editorSession(Astro.request)` and passes `session.token` — **the member wallet is authenticated by the editor identity.**

### The disagreements, resolved in one sentence each

- **Member auth exists or not?** Proposal 3 is right — the Go side is built and gate-tested; only the browser session and provisioning are missing.
- **One feature or four?** Neither extreme: **two** — Proposal 1's single feature would put a legally-gated money path behind a CSS token swap, and Proposal 2's split of "legal" from "identity" severs one causal chain (no brand → no opt-in → no wallet → nothing to sign into).
- **Task numbering `T300–T399` or a letter prefix?** Letter prefix — 004 is live at T200–T294 with 59 open and `speckit-converge` free to append, so a numeric range is a hostage to another feature's growth.
- **ADR number?** 0006 and 0007; Proposal 1 alone got this right.
- **Dark theme now or later?** Later — but Proposal 1's *internal ordering* (teach `contrast.test.ts` blocks and one level of `var()` **before** a single dark value lands) is a correctness ordering that holds regardless of any date and must be carried into the deferred feature verbatim.

---

## 1. Scope boundary — all 26 artboards, counted

**26 total = 17 apivo-news · 6 wholly evreos · 2 mixed · 1 documentation.**

### 1a. Wholly evreos — build nothing, ever, in this repo (6)

`LauncherClosed` · `LauncherOpen` · `LauncherDesktop` · `HomeMobile` · `HomeDesktop` · `Assistant`

`docs/master-prompts/evreos-browser.md` line 3: *"Planning artifact only. Nothing in this file is in scope for `apivo-news`."* The constitution (`.specify/memory/constitution.md:380–385`) lists "browser extension, mobile apps … or any further ecosystem mini-app" and, separately, **search** — which is why the `Αναζήτηση` rail item on `NewsDesktop` is also refused.

**On the 1 October critical path (6):** LegalDesktop, SignIn, WalletMobile, CatalogueMobile, MerchantMobile, WalletDesktop *(minimal: the approval-disclosure box only)*.

**Deferred to feature 006 (11):** Palette, Theme, Profile, ProfileDesktop, Settings, Faq, CatalogueDesktop, and all four news boards.

---

## 2. Spec-kit structure

Two features. Verified mechanics: `create-new-feature.sh` computes highest-existing `specs/NNN-` **+1**, creates a directory, writes `.specify/feature.json`, and prints `export SPECIFY_FEATURE=` — it creates **no git branch**. Real branches stay `xcoder/<slug>` (Principle I, enforced by `scripts/lint-refs.sh`), one small PR per issue. Feature count therefore places **no limit at all** on parallel agents.

Numbering: highest on `main` is 004 → next is **005**. PR #493 brings `specs/003-cashback-claims`, which does not change that. After 005 exists, the next is **006**. Do **not** pass `--number`.

### Feature 005 — `specs/005-pilot-launch`

**Acceptance criterion, one sentence:** *A German patient scans a QR code at the counter, creates an account, accepts the terms, opts into cashback, clicks out to the partner, and sees a pending entry in a wallet authenticated as them.*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Task ids** | `PILOT-T001` – `PILOT-T0nn` (≈70). Letter prefix, following the `CB-` precedent. Cannot collide with T001–T035, CB-T001–CB-T147, T148–T192 or T200–T29x, and cannot be broken by 004 extending its range. |

Specified during the pilot sprint, **implemented from 2 October**. Contains Palette, Theme, the deferred member surfaces (/profile, /faq, /settings), the news-board deltas, and the typed approver/publication contract change.

| | |

| **Task ids** | `DS-T001` – |
| **Milestone** | `M-DESIGN` — specified by 30 Sep, implementation opens 2 Oct |

Prepared by an agent via `/speckit-constitution`, ratified by the founder **once**, batching: the **PATCH** bringing Governance current with Q1 as amended 2026-09-03 (Awin + Linkwise), which 004 says is owed; and the **MINOR** adding claims plus C-8/C-9/C-10, which `specs/003-cashback-claims` is blocked on. A third clause — lifting "in-store cashback" off the out-of-scope list — is drafted **only if** founder decision #1 comes back "in-store", and that answer means 1 October is not achievable as planned.

- `docs/adr/0006-module-shell-seam.md` — the eight contract items, the three already satisfied by shipped code, the no-bridge URL fallback, the **unreconciled** inset arithmetic (44/74 on Main vs 92 above / 98 below on the launcher boards — record the ambiguity, do not resolve it), and the engine baseline. 8. **The `/[lang]/legal` index page**, keeping only `/imprint`, `/privacy`, `/terms`, `/contact` as deep-linkable routes; the footer anchors point at them directly.

the cashback API. `editorSession` is documented as "the editor identity behind the
editorial screens".

Merge #493 — it is the only copy of the member cashback UI — but **file this as a
security issue and land the fix as the very next PR, and do not publicly deploy the
cashback routes in between.** If the member session is not ready, the interim is to make
the route refuse rather than authenticate as an editor.

commercial-register/VAT identifier and the §18 MStV responsible person, then

**Wave B — days 3–9, inherently sequential, one agent, four ordered PRs.**
(1) `web/src/lib/member/session.ts` mirroring `editorial/session.ts`, including its
refusal to invent a placeholder name; resolved in middleware where identity already
resolves. (2) `/[lang]/signin` plus wiring the existing `/[lang]/register` form (every

catalogue string; `documents['privacy']` may be absent and must render without a version
line rather than printing `undefined`; then replace the dead `<span>`s in

004's **T254** to the top of 004's own queue: click-out does not today refuse a member
who never opted in, so a signed-in member with no participation can be credited.

(`t.confirmationTimeUnknown` is catalogued and referenced nowhere) plus `t.rateAtClick`;
and the withdraw page's three-line approval box, retiring the dead `approvalStep1/3`.

**Wave D — days 14–22, three parallel agents.**

660px; the wallet hero states `belowThreshold` plus a shortfall from a new
integer-minor-unit `shortfall()` in `money.ts` that throws on currency mismatch exactly

rewriting, and `PILOT-` cannot collide with T200–T294. The single intersection is T254,

Every new screen is the same small commits: strings module + its `.test.ts` (`el` and
`de`, keyed by the language axis, never a locale) → **add the module to
`coverage.include` in `web/vitest.config.ts` in the same commit** (its own comment is a
build instruction; unlisted files are invisible to the 80% gate) → the `.astro` page
taking every value from `modernist.css` variables → any Go endpoint with the test
asserting the *database* refuses → wire into `SiteFooter.astro` → a `data-tour` anchor
if it joins a tour.

- **`/[lang]/signin`** builds on `editor/signin.astro`'s working POST/redirect/GET and
  `isSameOrigin`; reuses `t.signIn`, `t.signInPending`, `t.emailLabel`,
  `t.registrationPending`, all already in both catalogues. Do **not** grow a sign-out —
  ADR 0007 assigns it to the shell — and do not add an `@epiloyes.example` placeholder;
  the lint's `HOST_PATTERN` matches it.
- **The legal pages** — entity, address, jurisdiction and support addresses are brand
  values and **must not be translated**; keep "Impressum · TMG §5" untranslated in the
  `de` catalogue because it cites a statute; all panes render signed-out.
- **The #493 deltas** — keep what the boards subtract: the wallet's four-tab filter row

  credit *and* its reversal to be visible); `t.shopAtTracking` / `t.opensTracked` (the

  it is recorded); the catalogue's `<label for="q">`. Add a `cashback.test.ts` guard

**Blocking engineering — needed in the first 48 hours:**

1. **Is the partner's price-lock offer an ONLINE click-out or an IN-STORE claim?**

   cashback and card-linked offers are on the constitution's out-of-scope list
   (`constitution.md:385`), there is no backend for escrowed partner funding, and
   `specs/003-cashback-claims` is itself blocked on an amendment. **Working default:
   online** — QR at the counter → catalogue → tracked click-out via Awin. If the partner
   has no online storefront on a connected network, say so now: the fallback is sign-up
   plus operator-entered goodwill credits from a named house account, which is a
   different feature, not a schedule change.
2. **Brand facts and the `BRAND_DIR` location** — legal entity, registered address,
   jurisdiction, three support addresses, and the deployment path. Blocks opt-in (503

5. **Ratify the batched constitution amendment** in one act (PATCH: Q1 Awin+Linkwise,

6. **Confirm the cut list** so it is not relitigated in week three.

8. **The three legal texts** (cashback terms, GDPR privacy notice, TMG §5 Impressum) —

   German patients is not a trade-off.
9. **The §18 MStV responsible person for editorial content.** This product publishes
   approved articles with named approvers, so the obligation is real.
10. **The commercial-register or VAT identifier**, which depends on the jurisdiction in 2.
11. **The retention schedule** the privacy notice must state.
12. **The freeze date. Working default: 25 September.** A freeze on 30 September is not
    a freeze.
13. **Wordmark colour sign-off** — the accessibility answer is not in doubt, but
    `--color-accent` → `--color-accent-700` visibly changes the footer wordmark, the
    editor chrome and the cashback bar. Do not let an agent land it silently inside a

**Risks, most decisive first.**

1. The pilot may be constitutionally unshippable as described — ask decision 1 today.
2. Legal-text latency sits on the money path, because no brand means a 503 on opt-in.
3. PR #493 is large, unmerged, and carries an authorisation defect.
4. Account provisioning touches the table the approval invariants depend on.
5. The privacy notice may claim more than the product can do (decision 7).

   consumes the same reviewers as the critical path — while carrying a 39/39 budget
   fight and a test-harness refactor. Every hour on it in September is an hour off the
   chain that closes the pilot.
7. Board numbers becoming contracts — land the errata early.
8. Issue-queue drowning: 004 already has 59 open. Generate 005's issues one phase at a time.
9. **Archivo ships no Greek subset** (#51) — Greek falls to `system-ui`, so the browser
   will not look like the Greek artboards. Decide whether that is acceptable.
10. 13 worktrees pinned to old `xcoder/cb-*` branches and a 773-commit-stale tree.
    Clean up before dispatching agents, or they branch from history.
11. `docs/demo-recording-prompt.md` is untracked and would be lost by `git clean`.

**Cut order.** Items 1–6 are *already* cut in this plan: everything evreos; the dark
theme and the whole Palette/Theme substrate; the typed approver/publication contract
change; `/profile` and `/faq`; `/settings` as a route; place chips, category chips, the

**Never cut:** the legal three, account provisioning, the wallet auth fix, and the

  `sh scripts/lint-refs.sh --from-messages origin/main..HEAD` before pushing.

Plan is written and revised. Here's what happened and what changed.

## The plan

**Two spec-kit features, not one**, split by the 1 October date:

- **`005-pilot-launch`** (`PILOT-T###`, milestone `M-PILOT`) — one acceptance sentence: *a German patient scans a QR code at the counter, creates an account, accepts the terms, opts into cashback, clicks out, and sees a pending entry in a wallet authenticated as them.*
- **`006-design-system`** (`DS-T###`) — specified during the sprint, implemented from 2 October: dark theme, `/profile`, `/settings`, `/faq`, the news deltas.

Plus three documents that are not features: ADR 0006 (the shell seam), ADR 0007 (the settings ownership split), and `docs/design/` vendoring the 26 boards with an errata file.

Of the 26 artboards: **17 are apivo-news work, 6 are wholly evreos, 2 are mixed, 1 is a decision board.** Only 6 are on the pilot critical path.

## Three findings that changed the plan after you approved it

I ran a 16-agent grounding pass over all 26 boards while writing; it landed after approval and corrected me on two points and found a defect. I verified all three myself before rewriting:

**1. I was wrong that member auth isn't wired.** I'd grepped only the frontend. `internal/identity/` verifies Supabase JWTs, and a `MemberAuthenticator` gates every route in five cashback packages, wired in `cmd/apivo/main.go`. What's actually missing is the browser session module (days) and — the real blocker — **account-row provisioning**: nothing in production inserts an `account` row, so a member who signs up gets a valid token and a 401 everywhere. That's a security task, because `account.role` gates both approval invariants.

**2. `BRAND_DIR` gates the money path.** `cmd/apivo/main.go:777` logs that without a brand definition, `POST /api/v1/cashback/participation` answers 503. The legal texts aren't a compliance chore beside the product — no brand → no opt-in → no wallet → nothing to sign into. That makes commissioning them the longest pole, and the only critical-path item no agent can produce.

**3. PR #493 authenticates the member wallet as the editor.** `wallet.astro:73` calls `editorSession(Astro.request)` and passes that token to the cashback API. Merge #493 — it's the only copy of that UI — but file this as a security issue, land the fix as the next PR, and don't deploy the cashback routes publicly in between.

## What I need from you first

**The one question everything is subordinate to: is the partner's price-lock offer an online click-out or an in-store claim?** In-store cashback is on the constitution's out-of-scope list, there's no backend for partner-funded escrow, and `003-cashback-claims` is itself blocked on an amendment. Working default is online via Awin. If the partner has no online storefront on a connected network, that's a different feature, not a schedule change — and 1 October stops being achievable as planned.

# Feature Specification: Cashback Claims — A Missing Credit Is a Record, Not a Ticket

**Feature Branch**: `003-cashback-claims`

**Created**: 2026-09-03

**Status**: Draft — blocked on a constitution amendment (see Governance Impact)

**Input**: Design handoff from the Apivo design canvas, turn 4, screens **4e**
(member: "Report a missing cashback") and **4f** (operator: claims queue with
evidence and our records side by side). The founder's direction on the handoff:
build the cashback screens against the shipped backend, and take the claim flow
— which has no backend — through the full spec process rather than drawing it.

## Governance Impact (blocking)

Constitution **v1.2.0** does not name claims. It is not that claims are
forbidden; it is that the "Cashback alpha" scope block lists what is in scope
and a claim handling surface is not among the items. Principle: *"scope stays
inside the declared product scope"* is checked on every PR, so an
implementation would be refused at review with nothing to point at.

This feature therefore requires a **MINOR amendment** adding claims to the
cashback scope block and adding the three invariants below to Principle IX.
The amendment is drafted alongside this spec; **implementation does not start
until the founder ratifies it.**

### The three invariants this feature adds

- **C-8 (No claim decision without a named decider)**: a claim decision row
  cannot exist without a non-null named human decider. The row IS the
  decision, exactly as `article.approved_by` is the approval and
  `payout.approved_by` is the payout's.
- **C-9 (Claim decisions are append-only)**: a decision rejects UPDATE, DELETE
  and TRUNCATE. Reversing a decision is a new superseding decision citing the
  one it supersedes, never an edit. The member's record shows both.
- **C-10 (A claim never moves money by itself)**: a claim resolution that
  results in a credit does so through the existing evidence-backed paths — an
  attribution of an already-ingested network transaction, or a goodwill
  posting from a named house account, recorded as goodwill. A claim may not
  write a `cashback.entry` citing evidence that does not exist, because C-2
  makes that unrepresentable, and it may not write a balance at all, because
  C-1 makes that unrepresentable.

## Product Frame

## Product Frame

The mockup's claim screen carries one sentence that decides the whole design:

> *A claim is a record, not a support ticket.*

A support ticket is a conversation that ends when somebody stops replying. A
claim is an assertion that money is owed, and the product's whole posture — for
news and for cashback alike — is that a claim on money carries a state, dated
evidence, and a named person behind the decision. The newsroom cannot publish a
sentence without a named approver; operations cannot refuse a member's money
without a named decider and a reason the member gets to read.

The mockup states the promise in the member's own words — "a named operator
answers within 5 days", and "the decision and its reason join your record —
either way". Both halves are requirements here, and the second is the harder
one: a refusal is recorded and shown as plainly as a payment.

## Why a claim cannot simply pay out

This is the constraint that shapes everything downstream, and it is worth
stating before the user stories rather than discovering it in them.

**C-2**: a cashback credit cannot exist without a reference to exactly one
network transaction record. So when a member says "I bought this and got
nothing", exactly one of three things is true, and they have different remedies:

1. **The network reported it and we failed to attribute it.** The transaction
   is sitting in `cashback.unattributed_transaction`. The remedy already
   exists: `POST /ops/unattributed/{id}/attribute`. The claim's job is to find
   it and point the operator at it. This is the common case and it costs the
   business nothing — the commission was already earned.

2. **The network reported it and attributed it, but at the wrong rate.** The
   entry exists and is wrong. The remedy is an adjustment posting citing the
   dated rate that should have applied — the same machinery a reversal uses,
   in the other direction.

3. **The network never reported it.** There is no evidence and there never
   was. No entry may be created: an entry that cites nothing is exactly the
   row C-2 exists to forbid. The remedies are to escalate to the network
   (which may later produce the transaction, at which point case 1 applies),
   or to pay the member **goodwill** out of a named house account — money the
   business spends, not commission it passes on. Goodwill is visible as
   goodwill in the member's record and in the accounting export. It is never
   dressed as cashback.

An operator who cannot tell these apart will reach for whichever button pays
the member, and the ledger will stop meaning anything within a quarter. So the
operator screen's job is not to collect a verdict — it is to **show which of
the three cases this is**, from our own records, before the verdict is offered.

## Clarifications

### Session 2026-09-03

- **Q: Is a claim a support channel?** A: No. It has a fixed shape, a fixed
  set of outcomes and a decision record. Free-text conversation with the
  member ("Ask the reader" in the mockup) attaches to the claim as recorded
  correspondence; it is not the claim.
- **Q: Can a member claim for a purchase where they never clicked out?** A:
  They can submit it, and it will be recorded and answered. It will almost
  always resolve as case 3, because without a click there is nothing for the
  network to attribute. The answer says so in those words rather than
  refusing the form.
- **Q: What stops a claim being a free money tap?** A: The decision is named,
  permanent and exported. Goodwill has its own house account, so the total
  paid as goodwill is a number somebody has to look at monthly rather than a
  rounding error spread across cashback.

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - A member reports a purchase that never tracked (Priority: P1)

A member in Munich orders €84.30 of groceries through a partner's tracked
link. Three weeks later the wallet still shows nothing for it. From the entry
list's footer — *"Missing a purchase? Report it"* — they open the claim form,
which already knows who they are and which partners they have clicked out to.
They give the partner, the purchase date, the amount and the order number, and
attach the order confirmation. On submit they get a reference immediately, and
the claim appears in their own record with the state "answered within 5 days"
and the date that promise falls due.

**Acceptance scenarios**

1. **Given** a signed-in member with participation active, **when** they submit
   a complete claim, **then** a claim row exists with a member-visible
   reference, a `submitted` state and a due date five working days out, and
   the response carries the reference.
2. **Given** the same member, **when** they open their claims list, **then**
   the claim is there with its state and its due date, before any operator has
   looked at it.
3. **Given** a claim for a purchase date more than the network's reporting
   window in the past, **when** it is submitted, **then** it is still recorded,
   and the acknowledgement says the window has closed and what that means for
   the likely answer.

Two answers land well, but one uncovers a hidden cost. Interim findings while the re-plan finishes:

**Linkwise approved with credentials in hand is genuinely good news.** It answers 004's Q11, takes Phase D off the "no field mapped without a recording" fixture gate, and means the online catalogue can carry real merchants on 1 October. It also formally changes a recorded decision — 002's Q1 says "**Awin**, and only Awin for the alpha" — so that becomes a PATCH clause in the amendment rather than a silent drift.

**In-store claim is already specified, which saves weeks.** It is exactly case 3 in `specs/003-cashback-claims`: *"The network never reported it. There is no evidence and there never was… pay the member goodwill out of a named house account."* The claim row, the four outcomes (`attributed`/`adjusted`/`goodwill`/`declined`), C-8/C-9/C-10, the operator queue and the accounting separation are all designed. In-store is a delta on 003, not a new feature.

**Two costs you should see now, before the plan argues about dates:**

1. **The constitution currently forbids it.** Line 385 lists "card-linked offers, **in-store cashback**" inside *"Do not build, do not scaffold, do not leave TODOs for."* Building the claim UI is scaffolding for in-store cashback, so the amendment has to lift that line — on top of the MINOR that 003 is already blocked on. One ratification act, but it is yours to make and nothing in-store starts before it.

2. **The receipt upload would be the first file upload in this codebase.** `git grep` for `type="file"`, `multipart` and `enctype` across `web/src` on both branches returns nothing. 003 also introduces an `EvidenceStore` port needing two working implementations (S3-compatible plus filesystem), object-storage credentials, and receipts are personal data under a privacy notice that does not exist yet. That is a capability, not a screen — and it is the single largest hidden item in "in-store claim".

There is an honest way around it for the pilot: the patient hands the receipt over **at the counter**, and the operator records its reference against the claim. No upload path, no evidence store, no new GDPR surface — and it violates no invariant, because C-8 only requires a *named decider*, which an operator is. I'll put that in the plan as the recommended pilot shape.

45 unticked tasks in 003 across seven phases, plus everything already on the pilot path. I'll give you a straight verdict on 1 October — not a hedge — when the eight-agent re-plan lands shortly.

### READING
HALF RIGHT, and the wrong half is the expensive one.  **Right: the German partner is the in-store path.**
`docs/master-prompts/evreos-browser.md` says it outright, twice. Under "Offline partners": *"partner
businesses (first, a German orthopaedic shop with thousands of patients and a partner-funded price-lock
cashback programme) hand their customers a concrete reason to install."* And dependency **D4**: *"Offline
partner campaigns — in-store claims, escrowed partner funding, per-campaign exposure caps. **Currently
excluded by the constitution** ('in-store cashback', 'card-linked offers'): the Orthopelma price-lock pilot
depends on this decision, **first on the web surfaces**, in Evreos second."* Plus the timeline line: *"The
partner's new shop opens on 1 October and cannot wait for a browser. The pilot runs on the existing web
surfaces."* So: in-store, on the web surfaces, on 1 October, gated on the same constitutional lift session
fact 3 already named. D4 is the founder's own name for the work.  **Correction 1 — orthopelma-website.md is
not evidence for this at all.** It explicitly excludes cashback: *"The price-raise and cashback/price-lock
campaign is **deliberately absent** from this site. The website pitch and the pricing pitch are separate
conversations."* and again in Non-goals: *"no cashback or pricing-campaign content anywhere on the site."* It
is a static Wix-replacement pitch built outside `apivo-news`. Do not cite it as pilot-cohort evidence; cite
evreos-browser.md.  **Correction 2 — "Linkwise = the online catalogue for Greek-diaspora members in Munich" is
not what 004 says, and the code cannot deliver it.** 004's own Q1 amendment splits the two networks by
**place**, not by diaspora: *"Linkwise is the Greece/Cyprus network; **Awin covers Germany**. Together they
match the product thesis — a Greek speaker in Munich — on both sides of it."* Awin is the German side.
Linkwise is the Greek side.  And the catalogue is scoped by place with an **upward** walk.
`internal/cashback/catalogue/queries/browse.sql`, `MerchantsForPlace`, walks `parent_id` from the reader's
place to the root; the seeded tree in
`internal/platform/db/migrations/0002_roles_withdrawal_costs.up.sql:371-376` is `Germany > Bavaria > Munich`
and **`Greece` as a separate root**. Munich's scope is exactly {Munich, Bavaria, Germany}. A Linkwise merchant
attached to Greece is invisible in Munich. The same file states: *"A merchant with NO `merchant_place` row is
available NOWHERE, deliberately."*  So the true statement is: **the German partner is the in-store path;
Linkwise is an online catalogue for the Greece place, and reaches a Munich member only if somebody decides
Greek e-shops attach to the Germany place.** That is an unanswered product decision, not a wiring detail. The
Greek-speaker-in-Munich thesis is carried by Principle VII on the *language* axis — Greek copy on Munich-
scoped merchants — and language is precisely the axis Linkwise's merchants do not travel on for free.
**Correction 3 — the pilot cohort is German-speaking, not Greek.** evreos-browser.md's persona: *"The partner-
referred member — **German**, often 40+, not technical, arrives via a QR code or a staff recommendation with a
cashback claim to redeem."* `NETWORK_LINKWISE_SOURCE_LANGUAGE=el` imports Greek merchant copy. Even with place
solved, the 1 October cohort would meet Greek names under a fallback label.

### LINKWISEIMPACT
 - **The registry does not ship Linkwise, and an unknown driver is FATAL.** `cmd/apivo/registry.go`'s
   `shippedNetworks` contains exactly one entry: `fixture`. `awin` is deliberately absent (the comment: *'It
   returns when it implements the port (T236-T241, deferred by founder decision of 2026-09-04)'*), and
   `linkwise` has no package, no `config.NetworkDriverLinkwise` constant beside `NetworkDriverAwin`
   (`config/cashback.go:45`), and no registration. `cmd/apivo/networks.go:139-147` on `networkAdapter`: *'An
   unknown name is fatal, unlike everything above it... starting anyway would leave a deployment that
   believes it is connected.'* So `NETWORKS=linkwise` today does not degrade — the binary refuses to start.
   Making Linkwise the default is not a configuration change; it is T242-T248 in full.
 - **Worse: Linkwise-as-default with no credentials takes the whole cashback product down.**
   `NetworkConfig.NeedsCredentials()` (`config/cashback.go:298`) is `Driver != "" && Driver != "fixture"` —
   so *any* non-fixture driver needs `NETWORK_<D>_API_KEY`. `CashbackConfig.Mountable()` is `Enabled &&
   len(UnusableNetworks()) == 0`, and `registry.go`'s `reportNetworkConfiguration` logs *'CASHBACK IS NOT
   MOUNTED: every cashback route will answer 404 and no member can click out'*. That is the founder's own
   2026-09-04 decision recorded in T217's divergence note (issue #513). With Awin absent, the pilot's
   fallback is `NETWORKS=` empty (cashback mounts, polls nothing, serves an existing catalogue) or
   `NETWORKS=fixture`. There is no third state where Linkwise is named and cashback still serves.
 - **The NETWORKS config block itself costs nothing — it is already built.** T215-T219 are all `[x]`.
   `internal/platform/config/networks.go` parses the ordered list, the per-driver blocks, refuses the five
   legacy flat keys by name, refuses duplicates and empty entries, and `credential_ref` is already per
   network. Making Linkwise the default is one line of env. **But the composition root still wires only the
   first entry**: `registry.go`'s `theConfiguredNetwork` returns `cfg.Networks[0]` and logs *'more than one
   network is configured and this build wires only the first; the rest are not polled'*. So 'default'
   currently means 'the only one that runs', and standing both online paths up at once is T220-T224.

   `conformAdapters()` returns `[]conformAdapter{conformFixture()}`. Every entry must supply four things
   only an adapter can know: a `window` that is inside the network's limits *and has transactions in it*, a
   buildable `deeplink` target, an `openUnmappable` adapter that meets a status word nobody mapped, and an
   `openReporting` adapter that can be made unwell. For Linkwise every one of those comes out of T242's

   and an unmapped status word. T231 (suite over the shipped registry) must land before T248 or the default

   real network the next catalogue import would mark them left_network - after members had clicked a rate
   that network never agreed to pay.'* So a Linkwise-default deployment has no seed path, and local

   Linkwise's publisher documentation is behind the affiliate login and `affiliate.linkwi.se/robots.txt` is
   `Disallow: /` for everyone. Every one of those three is a guess until Q11. That elevates **T261**
   (`Limits()` reads the network's row, per network) from hygiene to necessity: when the numbers are
   guesses, an operator needs to correct them with an `UPDATE` rather than a release.

   Linkwise publisher account, are credentials held, is there a sandbox? Its answer no longer decides

   founder said to forget the backend, which is about engineering effort. It does not touch this. One
   amendment covering both, prepared as a task and taken by the founder, is the cheapest path — but the in-
   store lift is what D4 calls for and 003's own status is 'Draft - blocked on a constitution amendment'.

   evidence?** 003's case 3 is 'the network never reported it', and its remedies are escalation or goodwill
   from a named house account. If an in-store purchase produces no network row at all, then `entry` is
   opened from a claim decision, and every invariant that reaches evidence through `network_transaction`
   needs to be re-read against that. This determines whether T200-T202 are sufficient or whether the claim
   path needs its own database rule.

   October.

   round trip. Linkwise's own `crl.js` enforces exactly five subid slots and research.md §5.3 lists *'The

   click and nothing anywhere reports it. This one unknown can invalidate the whole online path, and only an
   account answers it.

   mirrors it across cookie, localStorage and a server-side cache. research.md §5.4: *'It is a plausible
   join key in reporting, and possibly a better one than a subid.'* Which it is determines whether
   `IssuedClickRef` is carried at all or whether attribution runs through a value we do not mint. That is a
   port question, not an adapter one.

   label carry it? No task covers this and no task should invent an answer.

   makes it boot.

   `Mountable()` is satisfied, `lookupNetwork` still refuses. The intermediate state where Linkwise is
   'configured' and cashback merely does not poll does not exist; every state is either fatal or 404.

   in a German place, and the only German-place network is the one being deferred. If any part of the 1
   October pitch implies a German member can click out online, that is currently unbacked by any network,
   live or planned. The in-store path is the entire German offering.
 - **The empty-catalogue defect is silent and downstream of everything.** No production code writes
   `merchant_place`. A perfect Linkwise adapter importing five hundred Greek programmes publishes zero of
   them to any reader, and every diagnostic - import ran, routes created, offers priced - reads healthy.
   This is exactly the failure class 004 spends Phase 0 on, and 004 does not contain it.
 - **`allow_deeplinking=false` is the same shape of silence on the money path.** The member clicks, buys, the
   network pays the publisher, and only the member is uncredited. With Linkwise as the sole network this is
   not an edge case, and `can_attribute` (T207/T208/T245) is unbuilt.
 - **Governance is not waived by 'the backend will be there'.** Three separate gates stand: the constitution's
   in-store-cashback prohibition at `constitution.md:385`; 003's MINOR for claims plus C-8/C-9/C-10; and
   004's Q1 amendment, which the constitution's Governance section has not absorbed even for the 2026-08-31
   decision, let alone this one. Effort parallelises; amendments do not. Each is a founder act, and each
   must be prepared as a task now rather than discovered on 28 September.
 - **PR #493's authorisation defect is on the member wallet, which the in-store claim path terminates in.**
   `wallet.astro:73` authenticates the member wallet with `editorSession`. Any in-store claim that resolves
   to a credit is visible through that page. This is a pilot blocker independent of every network question.
 - **`BRAND_DIR` still gates the money path** (`cmd/apivo/main.go:777`): unset, `POST
   /api/v1/cashback/participation` answers 503, and the brand loader fails if the brand defines no terms
   document. A pilot member cannot opt in, and T254 makes opt-in a precondition of clicking out at all. Two
   independent gates on the same door.
 - **No production path inserts an `account` row.** A signed-up member holds a valid token and gets 401
   everywhere. This is upstream of participation, upstream of the wallet, and upstream of any claim. It is
   the first thing a pilot member does and the first thing that fails.
 - **FR-105 has a soft edge that will get leaned on.** It governs *money fields*. `Limits()`,
   `reporting_lag_minutes`, the deeplink parameter name and `allow_deeplinking` are not money fields, and
   research.md §5.2's primary-source evidence for the click URL, the five subid slots and the deeplink
   endpoint is genuinely good. The temptation under schedule pressure will be to call that enough. It is
   enough to write code against and not enough to ship money against, and the distinction is worth writing
   into the task text before somebody has to make the call at speed.
 - **Stalling 004 is not free even where tasks come off the path.** T203-T206 and Phase C are correct work that
   closes real money defects; taking them off the 1 October path means they land after a live pilot rather
   than before one, and the moment a second network is added they become urgent retroactively. Record them
   as deferred with the date, not as descoped.

# Revised build plan — epiloYES UI with both paths in scope

**Date**: 2026-09-05. **Refs verified against**: `origin/main` (20de06c), `origin/xcoder/cashback-web` (68377e2, PR #493).

---

## 1. What changed, and the three consequences that reshape the work

The founder decided, on 2026-09-05: **Linkwise is the working default network, and both online click-out and in-store claim are in scope for the 1 October pilot** — "forget about the backend, it'll be there." That last clause is about engineering effort. It buys agents; it does not buy a ratification, a network's reporting lag, or a reviewer's attention, and the plan below is built around exactly those three.

**Consequence 1 — in-store is 003's case 3, so the machinery is specified, not invented.** `specs/003-cashback-claims` (on `origin/xcoder/cashback-web` only) already describes the no-click, no-network claim as case 3, with escalation or a named-account payment as the remedies. `cashback.claim` has neither a `click_id` nor a `network_transaction_id` column — linkage is discovered at read time and frozen onto the decision's `records_snapshot` — so nothing needs relaxing to hold an in-store claim. `order_reference` is already nullable with a comment anticipating a shop that gives no order number. `cashback.merchant` is network-free (every per-network fact lives on `merchant_network`), and `cashback.merchant_place` already scopes on the place axis. What in-store changes is that a no-click purchase becomes a **first-class expected case with its own funding source**, not an exception paid out of our own pocket. That is a spec delta, not a new product.

**Consequence 2 — the constitution currently forbids it.** `.specify/memory/constitution.md:385` lists, inside "Do not build, do not scaffold, do not leave TODOs for": `card-linked offers, in-store cashback, multi-currency wallets, automated fraud scoring`. Separately, claims are not forbidden — they are simply **absent** from the Cashback alpha scope block, and "scope stays inside the declared product scope" is checked on every PR, which is why 003 has read "Draft — blocked on a constitution amendment" since 2026-09-03 with T148–T192 untouched. Two lifts are needed, in one act. Note also `constitution.md:369`: *"Polling is the only thing that creates a credit."* An in-store payment is created by an operator reading a till reference, so that sentence needs its companion or the amendment silently contradicts itself.
